_meta.note: DEMO / ILLUSTRATIVE DATA — historical event summaries used for model-validation display only. Statistics sourced from publicly available NDMA, IMD and published academic reports; exact figures may differ from authoritative databases.

events.name: Cyclone Fani

preEventConditions.notes: Extremely favorable oceanic and atmospheric conditions. Record-warm Bay waters (>30°C over large area) and weak wind shear enabled rapid intensification from Category 1 to Category 5 in ~36 h.

modeledRisk.notes: Demo baseline model correctly classified as CRITICAL. Risk score 94/100. Storm surge estimate within 0.3 m of observed.

observedOutcome.notes: Landfall near Puri at 185 km/h sustained winds. Record evacuation of 1.2 million people reduced fatalities. 10,000+ villages affected.

keyLessons: Early warning (72 h lead) allowed historic pre-positioning of relief
Coordinated mass evacuation saved thousands of lives
Coastal mangrove buffer reduced inland surge penetration
Power infrastructure most severely impacted — 11,000+ poles downed

events.name: Cyclone Amphan

preEventConditions.notes: Exceptionally warm ocean surface (32°C). Coincided with COVID-19 lockdown, complicating evacuation logistics. Rapid intensification from 120 km/h to 260 km/h in 24 h.

modeledRisk.notes: Model classified CRITICAL with risk score 97/100. Surge estimate slightly over-predicted at +0.3 m. Correct trajectory toward Sundarbans.

observedOutcome.notes: Strongest cyclone ever recorded in the Bay of Bengal at landfall. Kolkata city severely flooded. Massive economic losses in West Bengal.

keyLessons: COVID-19 complicated shelter-in-place vs. evacuation decisions
Sundarbans mangroves provided partial storm surge buffer
Urban infrastructure in Kolkata highly vulnerable to surge and wind
Economic losses disproportionate — dense urban and agricultural exposure

events.name: Cyclone Yaas

preEventConditions.notes: Favorable but not exceptional conditions. High tides at landfall amplified storm surge significantly — concurrent spring tide added ~1 m to surge levels.

modeledRisk.notes: Model correctly classified HIGH. Did not fully capture spring tide amplification in surge estimate (-0.2 m vs observed). Rainfall within 10 mm of observed.

observedOutcome.notes: Landfall near Balasore during high tide created worst-case surge. Successful proactive evacuation of 1.2 million people. Low death toll credited to preparedness.

keyLessons: Tidal timing critically amplifies or dampens storm surge impact
Mass evacuation framework from Fani/Amphan retained institutional memory
Odisha's cyclone preparedness model recognized as global best practice
Coastal embankments (bunds) breached in multiple locations

events.name: Cyclone Mandous

preEventConditions.notes: Weakening vertical wind shear and moderate SST prevented significant intensification. System weakened just before landfall due to increasing shear.

modeledRisk.notes: Model predicted MEDIUM risk (Category 2). Observed was Category 1 at landfall after late weakening. Conservative over-prediction is safety-appropriate.

observedOutcome.notes: Risk category matched (MEDIUM) but intensity over-predicted by one category. Conservative bias is operationally acceptable — better to over-warn than under-warn.

keyLessons: Late weakening due to wind shear is difficult to capture at 36 h lead
Over-prediction of intensity leads to unnecessary but safe evacuations
Urban coastal Chennai highly exposed to even moderate surge/flood
Drainage infrastructure in low-lying areas remains key vulnerability
